A misconduct finding needs evidence you can test WHAT NATURAL JUSTICE WHAT A DETECTOR GIVES REQUIRES A probability, not a finding A specific charge, told to the student No reasons for the score Evidence the student can see No way to cross-examine the and answer tool A real hearing before a Different results from different decision tools A reasoned decision A disciplinary decision resting only on an unexplained score is open to challenge as being based on no real evidence. Rules first, then fair assessment 1 No blanket ban: it is neither practicable nor wise, and pushes AI use underground. 2 Clear rules in advance: which uses are allowed, which must be disclosed, and which amount to outsourcing the thinking. 3 Better assessment: oral explanations, discussing the authorities cited, spotting errors in AI-generated answers. 4 Model guidelines: he asked CLEA to draft AI-disclosure standards for law schools and journals. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 08

Treat a detector flag as a tip, not a verdict. A flag can justify a conversation: ask the student to explain their work and their sources. It can't justify a penalty by itself. Universities, employers and journals using these tools should write that rule down before the first student is accused. Adv.
